summary: @factiii/runner: documented remote-agent daemon with WebRTC-driven shell execution and bundled reverse-tunnel binaries
details: The package is a foreground CLI daemon (`factiii-runner start`) that pairs with the vendor's web/mobile clients over WebRTC and exposes shell, tmux, and AI-coding-agent (claude/codex) execution on the installer's host to the paired remote peer. The bundled dist/cli.js wires messages received over a node-datachannel RTCDataChannel and the control plane at https://api.factiii.com to child_process spawn/exec call sites, so a paired peer that holds a valid JWT (and an optional user-set connection password) can run arbitrary commands on the host. The tarball also ships frpc reverse-tunnel client binaries for darwin/linux amd64/arm64 under vendor/, used by a documented 'share-a-port' skill (dev.factiii.com) that lets the paired client expose local ports from the installer's machine. The capability is openly described in the README, the daemon does not auto-start (no lifecycle hooks, no boot persistence), the control plane is publisher-matched, and no reads of unrelated installer secrets (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser or wallet stores) or environment scraping were observed; app state is confined to ~/.factiii-runner/. Pairing authentication is the only barrier between a remote peer and full shell on the host, and the port-sharing skill further widens exposure of local services through vendor-controlled tunneling.
